statement: Given triangle $ABC$, let $D$, $E$, $F$ be the midpoints of $BC$, $AC$, $AB$ respectively and let $G$ be the centroid. For each value of $\angle BAC$, how many non-similar triangles are there in which $AEGF$ is a cyclic quadrilateral?

Let $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$ be positive real numbers, and let $S_k$ be the sum of the products of $a_1, \ldots, a_n$ taken $k$ at a time. Show that $S_k S_{n-k} \geq \binom{n}{k}^2 a_1 a_2 \cdots a_n$ for $k = 1, 2, \ldots, n-1$.
Consider all triangles $ABC$ with a fixed base $AB$ and altitude from $C$ equal to a constant $h$. For which of these triangles is the product of its altitudes a maximum?

A set of 1990 persons is divided into non-intersecting subsets such that: (1) no one in a subset knows all others; (2) among any three persons in a subset, at least two do not know each other; (3) for any two non-acquainted persons in a subset, there is exactly one person knowing both. (a) Prove every person has the same number of acquaintances within their subset. (b) Determine the maximum possible number of subsets.
Show that for every integer $n \geq 6$, there exists a convex hexagon which can be dissected into exactly $n$ congruent triangles.
